methods.label: Write the transformations and simplify
methods.explanation:
Let \(H(x)=ax^2+bx+c\). Because its graph is a parabola, \(a\ne0\). Reflection about the \(x\)-axis changes \(H(x)\) to \(-H(x)\), so adding the translated graphs will subtract two shifted copies of the same quadratic.

First suppose the original parabola moves right five units and its reflection moves left five units. A right shift replaces \(x\) by \(x-5\), and a left shift replaces it by \(x+5\). Hence
\[
f(x)=H(x-5),\qquad g(x)=-H(x+5).
\]
Their sum is
\[
\begin{aligned}
(f+g)(x)
&=H(x-5)-H(x+5)\\
&=a\big((x-5)^2-(x+5)^2\big)-10b\\
&=-20ax-10b.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the constant terms cancel, and the difference of squares is \((-10)(2x)=-20x\). The result is a line with slope \(-20a\), which is nonzero.

If the original parabola instead moves left and its reflection moves right, the sum is \(H(x+5)-H(x-5)=20ax+10b\). Its slope is also nonzero. Thus in either direction the graph is a non-horizontal line, choice D.
